decisive_items: Revealed ascending aortic aneurysm with diameters of ascending aorta and sinus of Valsalva at 49mm and 40mm respectively
Revealed mild aortic regurgitation of the bicuspid aortic valve
Organized thrombus measuring 1 × 0.8 cm found at the left coronary cusp of the aortic valve, covering most of the left coronary artery's ostium
response.rationale: R1 integrates the core structural findings (bicuspid valve, ascending aortic aneurysm) and explains the thrombus as a complication, matching the full clinical picture. R10 captures only the thrombus, missing the underlying valvular and aortic pathology.

rejected.why: Only lists ascending aortic aneurysm, omits bicuspid valve and thrombus.
Marfan syndrome requires systemic features; no physical findings support it.
Thrombus is a complication, not the primary diagnosis.
Ehlers-Danlos lacks supporting evidence and physical findings.
Slow perfusion is a downstream effect of the ostial thrombus, not the diagnosis.
Cardiac thrombosis is descriptive but incomplete without valve/aneurysm.
Focuses on valve regurgitation, ignores aneurysm and thrombus.
Coronary artery disease is contradicted by 'without significant atherosclerosis'.
Coronary ostial thrombosis is a local finding, not the overarching diagnosis.
Only bicuspid valve, misses aneurysm and thrombus.
Aortic stenosis is not supported; regurgitation is present.
